+def _get_base58_encode_pairs(alphabet: bytes) -> 'List[bytes]':
+    # pairs[hi * base + lo] is the two character encoding of digits hi, lo.
+    # All pairs are laid out in one string, each followed by a byte that is
+    # not in the alphabet, so a single split cuts out every pair at once.
+    # Only b58encode calls this, and it keeps the result per alphabet.
+    base = len(alphabet)
+    unused = set(range(256)).difference(alphabet)
+    if not base or not unused:
+        return [bytes((hi, lo)) for hi in alphabet for lo in alphabet]

actions.reason: I took check_ir and removed more code to cut module load cost. The changes: dropped the itertools import, replaced the product fallback with a comprehension, removed the redundant memo on the encode pair builder, and folded the decode map builder into the decode table builder. Outputs were identical, but the gain was well under the 1% minimum: check_ir 0.9976, encode_ir 0.9982, decode_ir 0.9987. Removing the rest of the memoiser would likely add only about 0.2% more, still short of 1%. The per-call paths (one divmod per four digits in encode, five lane-merge steps for about 34 digits in decode, a double sha256) are already lean. I see no small, behaviour-preserving change left that clears the minimum, so I am not submitting a candidate.

journal.text:
I worked on check_ir in base58/__init__.py. I tried to cut module load cost by removing code. I dropped the itertools import and replaced the product fallback with a comprehension. I removed the redundant memo on the encode pair builder. I folded the decode map builder into the decode table builder. Same bytes out was the bar.

Outputs were identical, and build and guard were both ok. The gain was too small. check_ir went from 177810081 to 177386381, a ratio of 0.9976. encode_ir was 0.9982 and decode_ir was 0.9987. The required ratio is 0.9900, so the sandbox rejected it as no improvement. I gave up and submitted nothing.

Import-time trimming is near its floor here. Four edits moved the needle by a ripple, not a tide. The remaining cost is likely in the encode and decode loops, not in setup. That is expected, not measured yet.

Next I will count big-int divmod calls per output char in the encode path. I will check whether batching them is possible without changing any bytes.
